newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak president says culture minister should quit.
newsitem.headline: Slovak president says culture minister should quit.

text.p: Slovak President Michal Kovac on Wednesday called on Culture Minister Ivan Hudec to resign after striking actors occupied part of his ministry in protest at state interference in the arts.

Hudec called in police on Monday night to clear the ministry of the actors and their supporters, including opposition parliamentarians, who wanted to meet the minister to discuss conditions in Slovakia's theatres.
Hudec refused to receive them and then called in police to clear the building. The police later withdrew.

"If minister Hudec does not begin a constructive dialogue with the Slovak cultural community he will only prove that he is incapable of directing the ministry and the best solution to this problem is his resignation," Kovac said in a statement issued by his office.
Many theatres, including the National Theatre, have been on strike since last month in protest at what actors consider increasing state interference in their artistic management.
"It is deplorable that the artists of this country have to resort to even such methods to come into contact with their minister," Kovac said.
"He should be the example of cultivation, communication and dialogue and not...arrogance, intolerance and conflicts."
Relations between Slovakia's stage community and government have been strained since last summer when Hudec sacked the director and artistic director of the National Theatre.
Actors and other workers have since protested at personnel changes in many provincial theatres.
Kovac has often clashed with the government of Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar, once an ally but now a bitter foe.
